newsitem.title: ROMANIA: SOCCER-STEAUA TRAINER RESIGNS OVER TEAM'S FATE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-STEAUA TRAINER RESIGNS OVER TEAM'S FATE.

text.p: Dumitru Dumitriu, trainer of Romanian league and cup holders Steaua Bucharest, has resigned in a row with his boss over the future of their side.

"I decided to resign because of tensions with Steaua president Marcel Puscas, who wants to impose changes I don't agree with," Dumitriu said on Friday. "I decided it was better to quit before being fired."
Puscas, appointed Steaua club president earlier this year, has campaigned to wrest the club from the umbrella of the military, which has set him at odds with Dumitriu.
The Steaua (The Star) was created 50 years ago by Communists who seized power in Romania with Moscow's help after World War Two. It was subordinated to the army, according to Soviet-style rules.
"I don't agree with the separation of the soccer team from the Defence Ministry," Dumitriu said.
He argued that continued army patronage would guarantee the team's financial security against post-communist magnates, bent on reaping a quick profit from the team's successes.
"I don't want the club to be taken over by some nouveaux riches."

Dumitriu, Steaua trainer since 1994, has won the national league three times with his side and the Romanian Cup twice. Steaua played the European Cup for the past three years but never got beyond group level to the quarter-finals.
